Thanks Ben — taking point. High-level draft answers below, plus I attached the residency matrix and retention summary. Feel free to copy/paste into the Q&A to send to Orchid.

1) Residency options (AWS / GCP / Azure)
- Pin at listing: we can set a default region for the listing during onboarding (e.g., us-east-1, europe-west1, eastus). This ensures all customer traffic from the Marketplace listing is routed to that region unless the buyer requests alternate routing.
- Buyer-driven routing: buyers can select region at purchase and we route to the nearest compatible region; this is our recommended flow for multi-region buyers.
- Fallbacks: if the pinned region is unavailable we have policy routing to a compatible subset of regions (we disclose compatible regions in the listing).

2) Retention windows (typical defaults)
- Token & inference logs: 30 days by default, configurable up to 365 days for enterprise listings.
- Customer content (stored artifacts, evaluation sets): 90 days by default; can be reduced to 30 days via contract for regulated buyers.
- KV cache / ephemeral caches: retained for 24–72 hours depending on workload; not persisted beyond configured TTL unless explicitly enabled.

3) Deletion workflow & SLA
- Triggering events: customer request via support API, contract expiry, or explicit deletion request from the buyer's Marketplace admin.
- Standard SLA: file-level purge from object storage within 72 hours; index/metadata purge within 7 days; complete cryptographic tombstone + verification artifact within 14 days.
- Exceptions: legal hold or audit requests pause deletion; in such cases we provide a notice and expected resolution window.
- Verification: we produce a signed audit artifact (JSON export of deleted object IDs + timestamps, hashed verification) and can provide a cloud-native snapshot of deletion logs for buyer review.

Notes / caveats:
- For EU-specific obligations we recommend pinning to an EU region at listing time and enabling our extended 180-day deletion verification window if your procurement/legal needs additional traceability.
- For marketplace integrations we typically include a table in the listing page that lists pinned region, compatible fallback regions, default retention, and deletion SLA.

Attached: Orchid_Redwood_Residency_Matrix.xlsx, redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf

Hi Olivia — attaching the requested Q&A and a concise region/retention matrix for your procurement and security teams. Quick summary:

- We support pinning a region at listing time (recommended for EU-only requirements) and buyer-driven region selection at purchase.
- Default retention: 30d logs, 90d customer artifacts; configurable by contract.
- Deletion SLA: purge object storage within 72 hours, metadata/index within 7 days, signed verification artifact within 14 days. Legal holds are respected and will delay deletion with notice.
